summary.text: A sea cliff is a steep rock face cut by waves on a cliffed coast, also called an abrasion coast.
Waves gnaw a notch into the cliff's foot, leaving an overhang that grows until it collapses under its own weight, so the shoreline moves inland.
How fast a cliff retreats depends on the surf, the cliff's height, how often storm surges strike and how hard the rock is.

facts.label: Southern England chalk
facts.value: Retreats just half a centimetre each year

facts.label: Dead cliff example
facts.value: The Königsstuhl on the island of Rügen

items.prompt: Waves keep pounding the base of a sea cliff, carving a hollow underneath. What eventually happens?

options.label: The cliff grows taller over time
The hollow fills up with sand for good
The overhang above collapses under its own weight
The cliff slowly moves out to sea

items.explain: Waves cut a notch at the cliff-foot, the overhang grows as the cliff is undercut, and it finally collapses under its own weight.

items.prompt: You find an old cliff a few kilometres inland, covered in plants and grass. What does the plant cover tell you?

options.label: Waves no longer actively attack it
It is eroding faster than ever
It was built from piled-up beach sand
Its rock is too soft for waves to cut

items.explain: Vegetation covering a cliff is a clear sign of a dead cliff, where wave action against it has died down.

items.prompt: One cliffed coast is made of hard granite; another is made of rock that barely resists erosion. What tends to form at the foot of the soft-rock cliff?

options.label: A flat rock wave-cut platform
A deep wave-carved sea cave
A raised coastal terrace
A beach

items.explain: Resistant rock leaves a flat wave-cut platform in front of the cliff, but weak rock gets a beach there instead.

items.prompt: Chalk cliffs in southern England lose about half a centimetre a year. About how fast does Germany's Mecklenburg coast retreat?

options.label: About 1 centimetre per year
About 25 centimetres per year
About 2 metres per year
About the same as England's chalk

items.explain: The Mecklenburg coast recedes by about 25 centimetres a year, far more than the half centimetre of the southern English chalk.

items.prompt: Besides waves, what other process is almost as important in wearing back a rocky cliffed coast?

options.label: The pull of the tides alone
Plants growing over the cliff
General weathering of the rock
Rivers flowing over the edge

items.explain: On rocky cliffed coasts wave action is not the only driver of retreat; general weathering of the bedrock is almost equally important.

items.prompt: An old wave-cut platform is found raised well above today's sea. What has most likely happened to that coast?

options.label: The land was pushed upward by tectonic forces
Waves piled the rock up over time
The cliff above it collapsed onto it
Coral grew on top of the old platform

items.explain: Tectonic uplift of a coast can raise wave-cut platforms into coastal terraces, and their height reveals how much uplift happened.
